occurrences.finding: Controlling Person - Submit Controlling Person Form to Licensing within two days after a person becomes a controlling person. See TAC 745.901: The operation has two known controlling person's who have not been updated including the director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Controlling Person - Submit Controlling Person Form to Licensing within two days after a person becomes a controlling person. See TAC 745.901 (26 TAC §745.903(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver was observed grabbing a child by the clothing causing them to fall in attempt to redirect.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: Orientation to the child-care center was not completed before having acessing to the children for a substitute caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver left a child on the playground unsupervised between 10-12 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Comply with Standards: A substitute caregiver hired by the operation did not comply with the minimum standards while working at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employees Comply with Standards (26 TAC §746.1003(2))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation: A caregiver failed to report concerns of abuse to the department of family a protective service.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation (26 TAC §746.1201(5))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child was left unsupervised in a hallway for approximately 2 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervised Naptime Daily: A caregiver was observed asleep at naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervised Naptime Daily (26 TAC §746.2901)

occurrences.finding: Licensed Operations Required Fees: The operation has unpaid fees associated with background checks.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensed Operations Required Fees (26 TAC §745.509)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children: The caregiver did not demonstrate patience when relating to children in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children (26 TAC §746.1201(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver grabbed a child by the arm leaving a bruise.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Caregiver did not show good judgement by tugging/ arguing on/over a blanket with a child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not show proper self-control when redirecting a child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: Two hours of  renew annual transportation safety training is needed for all drivers and director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This law was evaluated with regard to an investigation and has been found to be in violation with the Minimum Standard Rules for Licensed Child Care Centers based on observations made at the operation, review of records and supporting documentation, and interviews with parent and caregivers.   By not checking the label, a caregiver was giving a wrong breastmilk bottle to a child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: This law was evaluated with regard to an investigation and has been found to be in violation with the Minimum Standard Rules for Licensed Child Care Centers based on observations made at the operation, review of records and supporting documentation, and interviews with caregivers and parents.  A child was able to get out of the room without caregiver noticed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child: A substitute caregiver served a child with food that he/she allergic to.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child (26 TAC §746.3301(i))

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: There was no Food Allergy Emergency Plan signed by parents and health care professional for a child who allergic to fish.  The plan was signed and dated after the incident.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: The assistant director did not make a good judgment by not provide a thorough orientation and/or provide enough information in order for a substitute caregiver to conduct the job efficiently. As result, the substitute caregiver unknowingly serves a child food that he/she allergic to.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not use good judgment when yelling and hitting children's hand as type of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance: Children confirmed that a caregiver slapped kids' hand and yell at them when they are not listening.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance (26 TAC §746.2803(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This law was evaluated with regard to an investigation and has been found to be in violation with the Minimum Standard Rules for Licensed Child Care Centers based on observations made at the operation, review of records and supporting documentation, and interviews with various caregivers.   A caregiver was giving a wrong milk bottle to a non-verbal child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Harsh, Abusive or Profane Language: This rule was evaluated with regard to an investigation and has been found to be in violation with the Minimum Standard Rules for Licensed Child Care Center based on interview with victim, parent, and caregivers.  Caregiver admitted that he said inappropriate word to a child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Placing Child in Locked or Dark Room (26 TAC §746.2805(7))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This rule was evaluated with regard to an investigation and has been found to be in violation with the Minimum Standard Rules for Licensed Child Care Center based on interview with victim, parent, and caregivers.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance. The operation did not make the parents aware of an incident that placed their children at risk on the day it occurred, notifying them three days later.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance. Two children were unsupervised for eight minutes when they left the classroom without the caregiver?s knowledge.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan - No Long Waiting Periods: Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance. The classroom had a period of inactivity for 19 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - No Long Waiting Periods (26 TAC §746.2205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance. A caregiver and a member of management did not demonstrate good judgment when they did not notify the parent of an incident that took place 38 minutes prior to the parent arriving for a family event.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance. The operation did not report an incident that placed two children at risk within the required two calendar-day time frame.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This rule is being evaluated as part of an investigation and was found to be in deficient.  A caregiver was not using good judgment while using her feet with shoe on to pat a child's back to get the child to sleep.  Other two caregivers witnessed the action but did not say anything to the caregiver or report to the management.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Minimum Standards: This rule is being evaluated as part of an investigation and was found to be in deficient.  Three caregivers did not know it was considered a form of prohibited discipline when using one's foot to pat on a child's back to get the child to go to sleep.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Minimum Standards (26 TAC §746.1203(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: It was determined by the Child Care Licensing Investigator that one caregiver did mention that she takes treats away from children such as bubblegum and candy as a form of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Storage for Individual Belongings: It was observed that children's blanket and sleeping pack are on the floor. Some of the blankets were touching each other.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Storage for Individual Belongings (26 TAC §746.4505)

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: It was observed that blue mats in the classroom were not label with child's name or number system.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Napping Floor Mats Marked with Sleeping Side Distinguished: It was observed that the blue mats used for napping were not marked or colored so that the sleeping side can be distinguished from the floor side.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Napping Floor Mats Marked with Sleeping Side Distinguished (26 TAC §746.4503(c))
